messages:
maya: ran a battery of stress benches on marabou12b (int4) vs int8 this morning. surprising outcome: int4 wins on cost and latency but shows higher kv fragmentation during mixed-length chat sessions. full numbers pasted.
tess: can you drop the summary here?
maya: summary: 1) median latency int4=85ms vs int8=110ms 2) cost per token int4 ~0.62x int8 3) kv_frag_ratio avg int4=0.52 vs int8=0.34 under mixed loads 4) occasional alloc_failures on int4 at ~95th percentile session length (>3k tokens)
eli: were these on the 48GB nodes or 80GB?
maya: 48GB pools, dedicated canary. workload: 60% short (<=128), 30% medium (500-1200), 10% long (>1800).
jia: that matches the trend we saw with another model. int4 allocator gets more small slabs and fragmentation accumulates. did you test enabling slot-compactor more frequently?
maya: yes: compactor every 30m baseline, moved to 10m and frag dropped ~0.12. prewarm of 1GiB slab on load reduced early spike but steady-state still higher than int8.
omar: interesting. Given cost delta, we should keep int4 as default but add a fallback to int8 for heavy sessions OR add a runtime flag that switches kernels when kv_frag_ratio > 0.6 on host.
tess: runtime fallback sounds more complex but safer. plan: A/B experiment - 50% traffic int4-only, 50% traffic int4-with-fallback. monitor OOMs, revenue-weighted cost, and quality diff.
eli: how do we detect the switch? metric-wise: kv_frag_ratio + alloc_fail_count. threshold heuristic: frag>0.65 OR alloc_fail_count>3 in last 2m -> switch to int8 for that request/route.
jia: adding per-request fallback is tricky because model binaries differ. better to mark session as "heavy" and route it to int8 variant. less contended but higher cost.
maya: routing approach is fine. we have an int8 variant in the model catalog (marabou12b-int8). Add routing rule: if request.max_new_tokens + prompt_len > 2200 OR kv_frag_ratio(host)>0.65 route to int8.
tess: add note: don't route if user explicitly pinned int4 via model param. respect user override.
eli: can we instead do a gradual degrade: try int4, if allocation fails fallback to int8 inline and return a warning header? pros: fewer upfront re-routes. cons: a failed allocation is noisy and could cause latency spike.
omar: prefer preemptive routing; fallback on failure as double safety. implement both.
infra-bot: Feature flag created: marabou.quant_fallback -> rollout controls available.
jia: runtime patch submitted: detect_host_frag_and_route (#12411). ETA review 6h. Patch adds metrics: kv_slots_free, alloc_fail_rate, frag_ratio_10s.
maya: benchmark script to reproduce heavy sessions:
```
python tests/bench/generate_stress.py --model marabou12b-int4 --mix "0.6,0.3,0.1" --seed 42 --clients 32 --dur 600
```
eli: for the experiment UI we need delta views: cost/token, p99 latency, OOM count, and generation quality (BLEU/ROUGE/QA accuracy). maya, can you add eval harness to compare int4 vs int8 on our regression set?
maya: on it. I'll run nightly job and post diffs. preliminary quality delta negligible on our eval set (avg answer score diff <1%).
tess: config changes: 1) add model-catalog flag quant_fallback=true 2) add route rule for heavy sessions -> int8 3) enable compactor every 10m on 48GB canaries 4) add soft-reserve 6% memory for marabou on 48GB pools
eli: rollout plan: start canary 5% with routing + metrics for 1h, then 25% for 2h, evaluate OOMs & cost. abort conditions: >2 OOMs per host in 30m OR frag_ratio increase >0.1 over baseline.
jia: also add a throttle on max_total_tokens for public routes: if combined tokens > 2500 reject with 413 and hint (same as earlier approach). I'll include link to docs.
omar: logging: attach generation kernel version and quant mode to traces so we can correlate quality regressions to routing.
maya: ran quick A/B sim locally: switching heavy sessions to int8 reduced alloc_failures to zero in the run but increased cost ~18%. Cost-weighted decision favors keeping int4 but routing heavy sessions to int8 seems net-positive.
tess: action items: maya -> add eval harness + nightly job (ETA tonight) jia -> land route detector PR and token-throttle (ETA 6h) eli -> set feature flag and canary cohorts (ETA 1h) omar -> schedule extra compactor runs on canary fleet (ETA 20m)
infra-bot: Canary cohort created: marabou.quant_fallback -> 5% (hosts tagged canary-48gb). Monitoring window 1h.
email-bot: FYI sent to product for cost impact summary.
maya: note to docs: explain quant_fallback behavior and how customers can opt-out by setting model param.
tess: nice work. let's keep an eye on long-tail sessions and update perf-evals to include mixed-length workload as default.
